edition: CDC Adult Immunization Schedule, Ages 19 Years or Older, United States, 2025 (Addendum updated July 2, 2025)
notEvaluated: Table 2 (by medical condition) and every 'Special situations' note: pregnancy, immunocompromising conditions, HIV infection, asplenia/complement deficiency or inhibitor use, solid organ transplant, chronic liver/heart/lung/renal disease, diabetes, cochlear implant or CSF leak, alcoholism, smoking

Occupational, travel and exposure indications: health care personnel, international travel, college students in residential housing, military recruits, laboratory workers, sexual exposure risk, injection drug use, incarceration, close contacts of immunosuppressed persons or international adoptees
Tdap/Td: 'Pregnancy: 1 dose Tdap during each pregnancy' and 'Wound management'; whether a Tdap dose was received at age 10 years or older (any Td or Tdap counts toward the 10-year booster)
Shared clinical decision-making recommendations (HPV 27-45 years, MenB 16-23 years, HepB age 60+ with diabetes, pneumococcal after PCV13+PPSV23 at 65+)
Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) and Mpox: indication-based only
Minimum intervals and repeat-if-too-soon rules: doses are counted by date, not validated against minimum intervals
Serologic immunity is accepted only from qualitative results (positive/reactive/immune); numeric titers are not interpreted

rules.reason: Age 19 years or older: 1 dose any influenza vaccine appropriate for age and health status annually.

Schedule: '1 or more doses of 2024–2025 vaccine (See Notes)'; the notes depend on product (Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech, Novavax, Janssen) and on doses before the 2024–25 vaccine, and the 2024–25 formula no longer matches the current season.

Schedule: '2 or more doses of 2024-2025 vaccine (See Notes)'; the notes depend on product (Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech, Novavax, Janssen) and on doses before the 2024–25 vaccine, and the 2024–25 formula no longer matches the current season.
Age 50–74 years: 'Unvaccinated and at increased risk of severe RSV disease: 1 dose' (risk-based, not evaluated).
Age 75 years or older: 'Unvaccinated: 1 dose (Arexvy or Abrysvo or mResvia). Additional doses not recommended.'
1 dose Tdap, then Td or Tdap booster every 10 years.
No evidence of immunity to measles, mumps, or rubella: 1 dose (if born in 1957 or later).
Evidence of immunity: Born before 1957 (except for health care personnel).
No evidence of immunity to varicella: 2-dose series 4–8 weeks apart (born in 1980 or later).
Evidence of immunity: 'U.S.-born before 1980 (except for pregnant women and health care personnel)'; GA does not record birthplace.
Age 50 years or older: 2–dose series recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) 2–6 months apart, regardless of previous herpes zoster or history of zoster vaccine live (ZVL, Zostavax).
All persons through age 26 years: 'complete 2– or 3–dose series depending on age at initial vaccination or condition' (fewer than 3 recorded doses not judged).
Adults age 27–45 years: 'Based on shared clinical decision-making, complete a 2-dose series (if initiated age 9-14 years) or 3-dose series (if initiated ≥15 years)'.

completeIf.reason: Adults aged 19 years and older who have received PCV20 or PCV21: no additional pneumococcal vaccine dose recommended.

rules.reason: Prior pneumococcal doses other than PCV20/PCV21: 'For guidance on determining which pneumococcal vaccines a patient needs and when, please refer to the mobile app'. With no prior dose: 1 dose PCV15 or PCV20 or PCV21.
Risk-based or on request: 'Any person who is not fully vaccinated and requests vaccination (identification of risk factor not required): complete 2–dose series HepA'.
Age 19 through 59 years: complete a 2- or 3- or 4-dose series (2-dose series only applies when 2 doses of Heplisav-B are used).
Age 60 years or older: 'without known risk factors for hepatitis B virus infection may receive a HepB vaccine series'; with known risk factors should receive one (risk factors not evaluated).
MenACWY: 1 or 2 doses depending on indication; MenB: risk-based, or shared clinical decision-making at 16–23 years (indications not evaluated).

Complete 3-dose series if incompletely vaccinated; 'most adults who were born and raised in the United States can assume they were vaccinated against polio as children' (childhood history not judged).
